purpose: Hand-authored claims of which theories/<Module>.v are checked, by a differential test, against the ACTUAL shipped production OCaml — not merely against the extracted Rocq model in isolation. This is a distinct question from 'is it proven': every theorem in proof-ledger.json is proven either way. It is the backlog-201 answer to 'model vs production' for this project, made mechanical rather than left to STATUS prose. scripts/check-production-link.py verifies each entry below against the freshly generated ledger and the named test file's real content (production_call must appear as a live reference, comments and string literals stripped).

ConvergenceSpec.note: Production link (specs/convergence-semantics.md §6): QCheck, 3000 RANDOMLY SAMPLED model terms per property, both modes. Each term is translated to a typed AST and run through the shipped Sarek_convergence.check_expr and is_thread_varying; the properties assert that production reports a barrier error iff the extracted check_env does, a warp error iff check_warp_env (ConvergenceSemantics) does, and that value variance agrees with is_varying_in_env. A production mutation (if-expression values back to uniform, C-2) fails all three. Covers only the model's constructor set: assignment, helpers, arrays, the intrinsic table and match are production features the model abstracts through EVary (ASSUMPTIONS.md), so the link says nothing about them. Sampling establishes agreement on the generated inputs, not universally.

known_gap: Only ConvergenceSpec is claimed shipped-linked, and only over the model's constructor set (see its note). ConvergenceSemantics' operational evaluator and soundness theorems are about the model; the link exercises its check_warp_env as an oracle but does not claim the module. Production features outside the model (mutable variables and control dependence, helper summaries, private arrays, declared intrinsic variance, match) are tested by fixed regression cases (sarek/tests/negative test_conv_*, sarek/tests/unit test_convergence_accepted) and not by a differential property.
